en.summary: Saudi Arabia's Cabinet rejected using vital waterways as tools of pressure or coercion, emphasizing that navigation through key maritime routes must remain free and consistent with international law.

en.summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni discussed bilateral cooperation and regional developments during a telephone conversation. Both leaders stressed the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation in vital waterways to enhance regional stability.

stories.title: ‎GACA issues classification for air carriers, airports in August 2026

en.title: GACA issues classification for air carriers, airports in August 2026
en.summary: Saudi aviation authority released a performance classification for airlines and airports based on passenger complaints in August 2026, with total complaints rising 4% year-over-year to 2,402.

stories.title: ‎TGA extends truck operational lifespan to 22 years for another 6 months

en.title: TGA extends truck operational lifespan to 22 years for another 6 months
en.summary: Saudi Arabia's Transport General Authority extended until March 26, 2027, a decision allowing trucks in heavy freight transport to operate for up to 22 years. The extension aims to help operators maximize asset value and manage their fleets more flexibly.

stories.title: ‎US to release 40M barrels of crude from SPR

en.title: US to release 40M barrels of crude from SPR
en.summary: The Trump Administration is releasing up to 40 million barrels of crude oil from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve as the final phase of a coordinated effort with the International Energy Agency. The release will occur through an exchange mechanism where companies borrow crude and replenish reserves later.

stories.title: ‎CMA seeks public input on earnings call controls

en.title: CMA seeks public input on earnings call controls
en.summary: The Capital Market Authority is requesting feedback on draft regulations for earnings calls, with a 30-day consultation period ending October 29, 2026. The proposed rules aim to enhance disclosure and transparency between listed companies and investors regarding financial results.

en.title: Amwaj International details 5 lawsuits seeking SAR 67.9M
en.summary: Amwaj International has filed five lawsuits in commercial courts to recover outstanding receivables and financial claims totaling SAR 67.9 million from customers.
